newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia clashes leave 3 soldiers, many rebels dead.
newsitem.headline: Colombia clashes leave 3 soldiers, many rebels dead.

text.p: Raging battles in east and northeast Colombia over the weekend left at least three soldiers and as many as 25 leftist rebels dead, army sources said on Sunday.
The latest fighting broke out on Sunday near the town of Restrepo in a mountainous area on the edge of the eastern plains about 40 miles (60 km) from Bogota.

Two soldiers died and six others were injured said an army officer, who did not wish to be named. He added that about 15 rebels, members of the 53rd Front of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), were killed, but said the exact number was difficult to verify because the guerrillas had dragged away most of the corpses.
Fighting ground to a halt at nightfall on Sunday but the officer said operations would resume at first light Monday.
In clashes last month, the 53rd Front of the FARC killed 16 soldiers as they disembarked from a helicopter in the town of San Juanito, a short distance across the mountains from Restrepo.
In separate clashes near the town of Tam, in northeast Arauca province, nine FARC rebels and one soldier died in heavy fighting in the northeast, regional army commander Gen. Rafael Hernandez said.
Fighting began shortly before midday on Saturday and continued through Sunday, Hernandez said. He said five soldiers were wounded in the clash, two of them seriously.
The FARC is Latin America's largest and oldest guerrilla army and was set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964.
If the deaths of the 15 rebels in Restrepo is confirmed, the death toll in politically related bloodshed will have risen to more than 70 since Thursday.

One of the bloodiest single incidents took place late on Friday near the town of Vegachi, in northwest Antioquia province. Eight men were dragged from their homes and executed by a 20-strong gang of suspected right-wing paramilitaries, authorities said.
